config.title: ::before and ::after

intro.title: ::before and ::after
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage element with decorative icons and text labels using CSS pseudo-elements. You will learn the core concept of using ::before and ::after to insert content before or after an element's actual content, without modifying the HTML. The main technologies involved are CSS selectors and the content property. This technique allows you to add visual enhancements purely with CSS, keeping your HTML clean and semantic. By the end, you'll be able to create custom bullets, icons, and stylistic flourishes.
intro.usecase: The ::before and ::after pseudo-elements are essential for adding decorative or functional UI elements without cluttering your HTML. Developers use them to create custom icons for buttons in dashboards, add visual separators in navigation menus, or insert required field indicators in forms. For example, you might add a small arrow icon after a dropdown menu item or a subtle shadow before a modal panel to enhance depth. This technique keeps your markup clean while enabling rich, maintainable visual designs across components like filters, tooltips, and data panels.

objectives: Implement ::before and ::after pseudo-elements on HTML elements
Configure content property values for generated pseudo-elements
Apply CSS styling rules to customize pseudo-element appearance
Construct decorative elements using pseudo-elements without modifying HTML
Manipulate pseudo-element positioning relative to their parent elements
Integrate pseudo-elements with existing CSS selectors and rules
Initialize pseudo-elements with different content types (text, icons, images)

steps.title: Understand the concept of pseudo-elements
steps.instruction: Read the explanation about CSS pseudo-elements and how they differ from pseudo-classes.
steps.hint: Pseudo-elements like ::before and ::after create virtual elements that can be styled separately from the main element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll understand that pseudo-elements create virtual elements for styling, while pseudo-classes style based on element state.
successCriteria: You've read about the purpose of pseudo-elements and how they differ from pseudo-classes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're getting there. Remember: pseudo-elements create virtual elements, while pseudo-classes style based on state.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: pseudo-elements like ::before and ::after create virtual elements that can be styled separately from the main element.

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for styling
steps.instruction: Add a div element with the class name 'target-element' to serve as the target for our pseudo-element styling.
steps.hint: Create a div element with a class attribute set to 'target-element'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with class 'target-element' is created, ready to be styled with pseudo-elements.
successCriteria: The code contains a div element with the class name 'target-element'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a div with the exact class name 'target-element'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The target element wasn't created correctly. Please add a div with class 'target-element'.

steps.title: Style the base element with basic properties
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to the .target-element selector to give it a width of 200px, height of 150px, background color of #f0f0f0, and center it with margin: 40px auto.
steps.hint: Inside the .target-element selector, add properties for width, height, background-color, and margin.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .target-element selector now has basic styling properties that define its size, color, and centering.
successCriteria: The .target-element selector includes width: 200px, height: 150px, background-color: #f0f0f0, and margin: 40px auto.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include all four properties: width, height, background-color, and margin with auto for centering.
steps.feedbackWrong: The base element styling is incomplete. Add the specified width, height, background color, and centering margin to the .target-element selector.

steps.title: Introduce the ::before pseudo-element syntax
steps.instruction: Add a ::before pseudo-element to your .target-element class. Include the required content property with a placeholder value.
steps.hint: Use the selector .target-element::before and set content to an empty string or placeholder text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .target-element class now has a ::before pseudo-element with a content property.
successCriteria: A ::before selector is added to .target-element with a content property defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a ::before selector, but make sure it includes the content property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a ::before pseudo-element to .target-element with a content property.

steps.title: Add content to the ::before pseudo-element
steps.instruction: Add the content property to your existing ::before pseudo-element with the text 'Before: '.
steps.hint: The content property is required for ::before and ::after to display anything. Use content: 'Before: '; inside your ::before rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ::before pseudo-element now has content, which will display the text 'Before: ' before the target element.
successCriteria: The ::before rule includes a content property set to 'Before: '.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the content property exactly as 'Before: ' inside the ::before rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content property is missing or incorrect. Remember that ::before requires a content property to display anything. Add content: 'Before: '; inside your ::before rule.

steps.title: Style the ::before pseudo-element
steps.instruction: Add CSS properties to the ::before pseudo-element to style it. Inside the existing div.target-element::before selector, add at least one property like background-color, width, or height to give it visible styling.
steps.hint: You can add properties directly inside the selector's curly braces. For example, you could set background-color: red; to make the pseudo-element visible.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ::before pseudo-element will have visible styling properties applied, making it distinct from the base element.
successCriteria: The div.target-element::before selector contains at least one CSS property that controls its appearance (e.g., background-color, width, height, border).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added something to the ::before selector, but it might not be a styling property. Try adding a property like background-color or width to control the pseudo-element's appearance.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::before pseudo-element still lacks styling properties. Remember to add CSS properties inside the div.target-element::before selector to style it.

steps.title: Introduce the ::after pseudo-element
steps.instruction: Add an ::after pseudo-element selector to your div.target-element class with its own content property.
steps.hint: The ::after pseudo-element works similarly to ::before but appears after the element's content. Add a new selector targeting div.target-element::after and include a content property inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see a new ::after pseudo-element selector added to your CSS with a content property placeholder.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a div.target-element::after selector with a content property inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the ::after selector targeting div.target-element and included a content property inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::after pseudo-element wasn't added correctly. Please add a div.target-element::after selector with a content property inside it.

steps.title: Style the ::after pseudo-element differently
steps.instruction: Add distinct styling properties to the ::after pseudo-element to make it visually different from the ::before pseudo-element.
steps.hint: You can use properties like background-color, border, margin, padding, or transform to create a clear visual distinction.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ::after pseudo-element will have different visual styling than the ::before pseudo-element, demonstrating how they can be styled independently.
successCriteria: The ::after pseudo-element has at least two distinct styling properties that differ from the ::before styling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but try to include at least two distinct properties that clearly differentiate ::after from ::before.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::after pseudo-element still needs distinct styling properties. Try adding properties like background-color, border, or margin to create visual separation.

steps.title: Use empty content for decorative pseudo-elements
steps.instruction: Change the content property to an empty string for both the ::before and ::after pseudo-elements to use them as purely visual decorations.
steps.hint: Set content: ''; in both pseudo-element rules. This creates invisible elements that can still be styled with borders, backgrounds, etc.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both pseudo-elements will have content: ''; set, making them suitable for decorative styling without adding visible text.
successCriteria: The ::before and ::after pseudo-elements have content: ''; property set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've set empty content for one pseudo-element. Make sure both ::before and ::after have content: '';.
steps.feedbackWrong: The pseudo-elements should have empty content. Set content: ''; for both ::before and ::after.

steps.title: Position pseudo-elements absolutely
steps.instruction: Add position: absolute to both the ::before and ::after pseudo-elements in your CSS.
steps.hint: Use the position property with the value 'absolute' inside both pseudo-element selectors.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both pseudo-elements will have position: absolute applied, preparing them for precise placement.
successCriteria: The CSS contains position: absolute in both div.target-element::before and div.target-element::after selectors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added position: absolute to one pseudo-element, but both need it. Make sure to add it to both ::before and ::after.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding position: absolute to both pseudo-elements. Check that you've included it in both selectors.

steps.title: Create shapes with pseudo-elements
steps.instruction: In the ::before pseudo-element, add CSS properties to create a circle shape using width, height, border-radius, and background-color.
steps.hint: Set width and height to equal values (e.g., 20px) and border-radius to 50% to make a circle. Add a background-color to make it visible.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ::before pseudo-element should display as a colored circle when you preview the page.
successCriteria: The ::before pseudo-element has width, height, border-radius: 50%, and a background-color property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all the necessary properties: width, height, border-radius: 50%, and background-color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ::before pseudo-element doesn't have the required properties to form a circle. Review the hint and try again.

steps.title: Combine ::before and ::after for complex effects
steps.instruction: In the existing div.target-element rule, add a background color to create a base for the layered pseudo-elements.
steps.hint: Add a background-color property inside the div.target-element selector to provide a visual base for the pseudo-elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The target element will have a visible background color, serving as a foundation for the layered pseudo-elements.
successCriteria: The div.target-element selector contains a background-color property with a valid color value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a background-color property with a valid color value inside the div.target-element selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The base element doesn't have a background color yet. Add a background-color property to the div.target-element selector.
